analysis:
All four changed files are test-only under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Live. No production source is modified, and the changes touch no trust boundary, key handling, attestation, authorization, or network contract.

1. GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift (head line 265): adds a `.toolCallDelta` case to the stream-event switch, required for exhaustiveness after an upstream enum addition. It records an Issue if a named tool_choice call is streamed. This only adds an assertion, and the live tests remain gated by DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_TESTS and DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_GEMMA.

2. Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift (head lines 389-391): handles `.toolCallDelta` by appending `delta.completed` to the collected tool calls. This is test collection logic only.

3. ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture.swift (lines 41-53): when a solo-prefill stripe is pinned, the fixture also pins DARKBLOOM prefill chunk and step token budget env keys from the default CBv2SchedulerConfig values. This is benchmark and qualification fixture geometry. The environment still contains only the isolated test root and ephemeral or test-persistent key flags. The persistent-key and isolated-root checks at lines 83-93 are unchanged. This relates to T-041 only as test infrastructure and does not loosen the production gate, TTL, HMAC naming, or DBK3 metadata.

4. ModelCheckpointStorageSpecificationTests.swift (lines 75-76): adds assertions for the new chunk (512) and step budget (2048) env values. The no-ambient-override test at lines 64-69 still checks that precision keys are not inherited.

No regression to T-041/SEC-035 or any other threat was identified. Residual limits: I did not see the EngineV2Factory key definitions or the upstream `.toolCallDelta` enum, so I could not verify them. Neither affects a security conclusion.
